div.head: Grið 24
div.ab: 7 wise eac wæron on geardagum woroldwitan, þe ærest gesettan to godcundan rihtlagan woroldlaga biscpan 7 gehalgedan heapan 7 haligdom 7 hadas for Godes lufan weorðedan 7 Godes hus 7 Godes þeowas deoplice griðedan.

And wise eac wæron on geardagum woroldwitan þe ærest gesettan to godcundan rihtlagan woroldlaga biscpan and gehalgedan heapan, and haligdom and hadas for Godes lufan weorðedan, and Godes hus and Godes þeowas deoplice griðedan.

Und weise waren auch in einstigen Tagen die Staatsregenten, welche zuerst zu geistlichen Rechtsgesetzen staatliche Privilegien aufstellten für Bischöfe und geweihte Convente, und Heiligthum und Kleriker aus Liebe zu Gott ehrten und Gotteshäuser und Gottesdiener mit tiefem Sonderfrieden schützten.

And wise too in days of old were the secular rulers who first added secular privileges to the spiritual laws for bishops and consecrated communities, and honoured the sanctuary and the clergy for the love of God, and protected God's houses and God's servants with deep special peace.

And wise also were the councilors in former days who first added secular laws to the just ecclesiastical canons for bishops and holy assemblies, and venerated sanctity and the holy orders for the love of God, and steadfastly protected God’s house and God’s servants.

note.quote: Hadbot and Grið, the latter probably drawing upon the former [n. Had. 11, Grið 24 – 25]

note.label: extends
note.quote: yet another reflection on the wisdom of former law-makers ... which extended, so was presumably a bit later than, the Hadbot version

div.note: Liebermann compares Had 11 and VIII Atr.; T: corrected against Rabin, DOML 66 (2020), p. 28 (before: ‘And wise eac wæron on geardagum woroldwitan þe aræst gesettan to godcundan rihtlagan woroldlaga biscpan and gehalgedan heapan, and haligdom and hadas for Godes lufan weorðedan and Godes hus and Godes þeowas deoplice griðedan.’)
